﴿وَإِذَا تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ قَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلْحَقِّ لَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ هَذَا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ يسمّون القرآن سحرًا.

﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَرَاهُ﴾ أي إن محمدًا افتراه من تلقاء نفسه. فقال الله عز وجل: ﴿قُلْ إِنِ افْتَرَيْتُهُ فَلَا تَمْلِكُونَ لِي مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا﴾ أي لا تقدرون أن تردّوا عني عذابه إن عذّبني على افترائي، فكيف أفتري على الله من أجلكم. ﴿هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ﴾ أي تخوضون فيه من تكذيب بالقرآن والقول فيه إنه سحر.

﴿قُلْ مَا كُنْتُ بِدْعًا مِنَ الرُّسُلِ﴾ أي بديعًا، مثل: نِصْف ونَصِيف، وجمع البِدْع أَبْداع. أي لستُ بأول مرسَل، قد بُعث قبلي كثير من الأنبياء، فكيف تنكرون نبوتي.

﴿وَمَا أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلَا بِكُمْ﴾ اختلف العلماء في معنى هذه الآية:

فقال بعضهم: معناه ما أدري ما يُفعل بي ولا بكم يوم القيامة. فلما نزلت هذه الآية فرح المشركون، فقالوا: واللات والعزى، ما أمرنا وأمر محمد عند الله إلا واحد، وما له علينا من مزية وفضل، ولولا أنه ابتدع ما يقوله من ذات نفسه لأخبره الذي بعثه بما يُفعل به. فأنزل الله: "لِيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللَّهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِكَ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ" [الفتح: ٢]، فقالت الصحابة: هنيئًا لك يا نبي الله، قد علمنا ما يُفعل بك، فماذا يُفعل بنا؟ فأنزل الله تعالى: ﴿لِيُدْخِلَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ جَنَّاتٍ﴾ الآية [الفتح: ٥]، وأنزل: "وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ فَضْلًا كَبِيرًا" [الأحزاب: ٤٧]، فبيّن الله تعالى ما يُفعل به وبهم. وهذا قول أنس وقتادة والحسن وعكرمة، قالوا: إنما قال هذا قبل أن يُخبر بغفران ذنبه [وإنما أُخبر بغفران ذنبه] [[ما بين القوسين زيادة من "ب".]] عام الحديبية، فنُسخ ذلك [[انظر: الطبري: ٢٦ / ٧، تفسير ابن كثير: ٤ / ١٥٦، القرطبي: ١٦ / ١٨٥.]].

أخبرنا أحمد بن عبد الله الصالحي، أخبرنا أبو الحسين علي بن محمد بن عبد الله بن بِشْران، أخبرنا إسماعيل بن محمد الصفّار، حدثنا أحمد بن منصور الرمادي، حدثنا عبد الرزاق، أخبرنا معمر عن الزهري، عن خارجة بن زيد قال: كانت أم العلاء الأنصارية تقول: لما قدم المهاجرون المدينة اقترعت الأنصار على سكناهم، قالت: [فطار لنا] [[في "أ" (فشاركنا) وفي "المصنف": فصار لنا.]] عثمان بن مظعون في السكنى، فمرض فمرّضناه، ثم توفي، فجاء رسول الله ﷺ فدخل، فقلت: رحمة الله عليك أبا السائب، فشهادتي قد أكرمك الله. فقال النبي ﷺ: "وما يدريك أن الله قد أكرمه؟" فقلت: لا والله، لا أدري. فقال النبي ﷺ: "أما هو فقد أتاه اليقين من ربه، وإني لأرجو له الخير، والله ما أدري وأنا رسول الله ما يُفعل بي ولا بكم". قالت: فوالله لا أزكّي بعده أحدًا أبدًا. قالت: ثم رأيت لعثمان بعد في النوم عينًا تجري، فقصصتها على رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: "ذاك عمله" [[أخرجه عبد الرزاق في الجامع للإمام معمر، المصنف: ١١ / ٢٣٧، والبخاري في التعبير، باب العين الجارية في المنام: ١٢ / ٤١٠، والمصنف في شرح السنة: ١٢ / ٢٤٣-٢٤٤.]].

وقال جماعة: قوله "وَمَا أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلَا بِكُمْ" في الدنيا، أما في الآخرة فقد علم أنه في الجنة، وأن من كذّبه فهو في النار. ثم اختلفوا فيه:

قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: لما اشتد البلاء بأصحاب رسول الله ﷺ رأى رسول الله ﷺ فيما يرى النائم، وهو بمكة، أرضًا ذات سِباخ ونخل رُفعت له، يهاجر إليها، فقال له أصحابه: متى تهاجر إلى الأرض التي أُريتَ؟ فسكت، فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية: "وَمَا أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلَا بِكُمْ"، أأُترك في مكاني أم أخرج وإياكم إلى الأرض التي رُفعت لي [[انظر: أسباب النزول للواحدي: ص ٤٣٩، القرطبي: ١٦ / ١٨٦-١٨٧.]]؟

وقال بعضهم: "وَمَا أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلَا بِكُمْ" إلى ماذا يصير أمري وأمركم في الدنيا، بأن أُقيم معكم في مكانكم أم أُخرَج كما أُخرجت الأنبياء من قبلي، أم أُقتل كما قُتل الأنبياء من قبلي، وأنتم أيها المصدقون لا أدري تُخرجون معي أم تُتركون، أم ماذا يُفعل بكم [وأنتم] [[ساقط من "ب".]] أيها المكذبون، أتُرمَون بالحجارة من السماء أم يُخسَف بكم، أم أي شيء يُفعل بكم، مما فُعل بالأمم المكذبة؟

ثم أخبر الله عز وجل أنه يُظهر دينه على الأديان، فقال: "هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدَى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ" [الصف: ٩]، وقال في أمته: "وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَأَنْتَ فِيهِمْ وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ مُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ" [الأنفال: ٣٣]، فأخبر الله ما يُصنع به وبأمته. هذا قول السدّي.

فقال بعضهم: معناه ما أدري ما يُفعل بي ولا بكم يوم القيامة. فلما نزلت هذه الآية فرح المشركون، فقالوا: واللات والعزى، ما أمرنا وأمر محمد عند الله إلا واحد، وما له علينا من مزية وفضل، ولولا أنه ابتدع ما يقوله من ذات نفسه لأخبره الذي بعثه بما يُفعل به. فأنزل الله: "لِيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللَّهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِكَ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ" [الفتح: ٢]، فقالت الصحابة: هنيئًا لك يا نبي الله، قد علمنا ما يُفعل بك، فماذا يُفعل بنا؟ فأنزل الله تعالى: ﴿لِيُدْخِلَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ جَنَّاتٍ﴾ الآية [الفتح: ٥]، وأنزل: "وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ فَضْلًا كَبِيرًا" [الأحزاب: ٤٧]، فبيّن الله تعالى ما يُفعل به وبهم. وهذا قول أنس وقتادة والحسن وعكرمة، قالوا: إنما قال هذا قبل أن يُخبر بغفران ذنبه [وإنما أُخبر بغفران ذنبه] [[ما بين القوسين زيادة من "ب".]] عام الحديبية، فنُسخ ذلك [[انظر: الطبري: ٢٦ / ٧، تفسير ابن كثير: ٤ / ١٥٦، القرطبي: ١٦ / ١٨٥.]].

أخبرنا أحمد بن عبد الله الصالحي، أخبرنا أبو الحسين علي بن محمد بن عبد الله بن بِشْران، أخبرنا إسماعيل بن محمد الصفّار، حدثنا أحمد بن منصور الرمادي، حدثنا عبد الرزاق، أخبرنا معمر عن الزهري، عن خارجة بن زيد قال: كانت أم العلاء الأنصارية تقول: لما قدم المهاجرون المدينة اقترعت الأنصار على سكناهم، قالت: [فطار لنا] [[في "أ" (فشاركنا) وفي "المصنف": فصار لنا.]] عثمان بن مظعون في السكنى، فمرض فمرّضناه، ثم توفي، فجاء رسول الله ﷺ فدخل، فقلت: رحمة الله عليك أبا السائب، فشهادتي قد أكرمك الله. فقال النبي ﷺ: "وما يدريك أن الله قد أكرمه؟" فقلت: لا والله، لا أدري. فقال النبي ﷺ: "أما هو فقد أتاه اليقين من ربه، وإني لأرجو له الخير، والله ما أدري وأنا رسول الله ما يُفعل بي ولا بكم". قالت: فوالله لا أزكّي بعده أحدًا أبدًا. قالت: ثم رأيت لعثمان بعد في النوم عينًا تجري، فقصصتها على رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: "ذاك عمله" [[أخرجه عبد الرزاق في الجامع للإمام معمر، المصنف: ١١ / ٢٣٧، والبخاري في التعبير، باب العين الجارية في المنام: ١٢ / ٤١٠، والمصنف في شرح السنة: ١٢ / ٢٤٣-٢٤٤.]].

وقال جماعة: قوله "وَمَا أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلَا بِكُمْ" في الدنيا، أما في الآخرة فقد علم أنه في الجنة، وأن من كذّبه فهو في النار. ثم اختلفوا فيه:

قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: لما اشتد البلاء بأصحاب رسول الله ﷺ رأى رسول الله ﷺ فيما يرى النائم، وهو بمكة، أرضًا ذات سِباخ ونخل رُفعت له، يهاجر إليها، فقال له أصحابه: متى تهاجر إلى الأرض التي أُريتَ؟ فسكت، فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية: "وَمَا أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلَا بِكُمْ"، أأُترك في مكاني أم أخرج وإياكم إلى الأرض التي رُفعت لي [[انظر: أسباب النزول للواحدي: ص ٤٣٩، القرطبي: ١٦ / ١٨٦-١٨٧.]]؟

وقال بعضهم: "وَمَا أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلَا بِكُمْ" إلى ماذا يصير أمري وأمركم في الدنيا، بأن أُقيم معكم في مكانكم أم أُخرَج كما أُخرجت الأنبياء من قبلي، أم أُقتل كما قُتل الأنبياء من قبلي، وأنتم أيها المصدقون لا أدري تُخرجون معي أم تُتركون، أم ماذا يُفعل بكم [وأنتم] [[ساقط من "ب".]] أيها المكذبون، أتُرمَون بالحجارة من السماء أم يُخسَف بكم، أم أي شيء يُفعل بكم، مما فُعل بالأمم المكذبة؟

ثم أخبر الله عز وجل أنه يُظهر دينه على الأديان، فقال: "هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدَى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ" [الصف: ٩]، وقال في أمته: "وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَأَنْتَ فِيهِمْ وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ مُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ" [الأنفال: ٣٣]، فأخبر الله ما يُصنع به وبأمته. هذا قول السدّي.

﴿إِنْ أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا مَا يُوحَى إِلَيَّ﴾ أي ما أتّبع إلا القرآن، ولا أبتدع من عندي شيئًا، ﴿وَمَا أَنَا إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 10:

﴿Say: "Have you considered?"﴾ Its meaning: "Tell me what you say, ﴿if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it﴾," O polytheists, ﴿and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like﴾. Al-mithl (المِثْلُ) is an extra particle (ṣilah), meaning "upon it," that is, upon the fact that it is from Allah. ﴿And he believed﴾, meaning the witness, ﴿and you were arrogant﴾ toward belief in it. The response to his saying, "if it is from Allah," is omitted, with the implied meaning: "Have you not then done wrong?" This omitted part is indicated by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾. Al-Hasan said: its response is "Who is more astray than you?", as He said in Surat as-Sajdah.

They differed concerning this witness. Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: he is ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, who testified to the prophethood of the Chosen One (ﷺ) and believed in him, while the Jews were arrogant and did not believe.

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Munir related to us, having heard ʿAbd Allah ibn Bukayr, Humayd related to us, from Anas, who said: "ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam heard of the arrival of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was in a field picking dates. He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'I am going to ask you about three things that none knows except a prophet: What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food of the people of Paradise? And why does the child resemble its father or its mother?' He said: 'Jibril has just informed me of them.' He said: 'Jibril?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'That is the enemy of the Jews among the angels.' Then he recited this verse: 'Say: whoever is an enemy to Jibril, indeed he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah' [al-Baqarah: 97]. As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather the people from the east to the west. As for the first food that the people of Paradise will eat, it is the extra piece of the fish's liver. When the man's water precedes the woman's water, the child resembles the man, and when the woman's water precedes, she [the child] resembles her." He said: "I testify that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah. [O Messenger of Allah,] [[What is between the brackets is missing from manuscript 'A'.]] The Jews are a people of slander, and if they learn of my Islam before you ask them, they will slander me." The Jews came, and he said: "What kind of man is ʿAbd Allah among you?" They said: "The best of us and the son of the best of us, and our master and the son of our master." He said: "Do you see if ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam accepts Islam?" They said: "May Allah protect him from that." Then ʿAbd Allah came out and said: "I testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." They said: "He is the worst of us and the son of the worst of us," and they belittled him. He said: "This is what I was afraid of, O Messenger of Allah."" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir (Tafsir Surat al-Baqarah), chapter: "Whoever is an enemy to Jibril" 8/165, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/372-373.]]

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us, saying: I heard Malik narrate from Abu al-Nadr, the client of ʿUmar ibn ʿUbayd Allah, from ʿAmir ibn Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, who said: "I did not hear the Prophet (ﷺ) say to anyone walking on the face of the earth that he is among the people of Paradise, except to ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, and concerning him this verse was revealed: 'And a witness from the Children of Israel testified to its like.'" He said: "I do not know whether Malik said 'the verse' or 'in the hadith'." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Manaqib al-Sahabah, chapter: Manaqib of ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, may Allah be pleased with him, 7/128; by Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter: Virtues of ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, may Allah be pleased with him, no. (2483), 4/1930; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/189-190.]]

Others said: the witness is Musa ibn ʿImran. [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/57-58.]]

Al-Sha'bi said: Masruq said concerning this verse: "By Allah, it was not revealed concerning ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, because Ha Mim (حم) was revealed in Makkah, while ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam accepted Islam in Madinah. This verse was revealed concerning a dispute that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had with his people. The likeness of the Qur'an is the Torah: Musa testified to the Torah, and Muhammad (ﷺ) testified to the Furqan, and each confirms the other." [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 26/9-10, and he said, favoring (26/10): "The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is that what Masruq said about the interpretation of this is more consistent with the outward sense of the revelation," because His saying "Say: have you considered, if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like" is in the context of Allah's rebuke of the polytheists of Quraysh and an argument for His Prophet (ﷺ) against them. This verse is similar to the verses before it, and no mention of the People of the Book or the Jews has preceded it, so this verse is directed to those who are among them. Nothing indicates that the speech has turned away from the stories of those previously mentioned. However, reports have come from a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that it means ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, and most of the people of ta'wil (interpretation) hold this view, and they were more knowledgeable about the meanings of the Qur'an, the cause of its revelation, and what was intended by it. So the meaning of the speech, given that this is the case, is: "ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, who is the witness from the Children of Israel, testified to its like," meaning to the likeness of the Qur'an, which is the Torah, and that testimony is his testimony that Muhammad is written in the Torah as a prophet, which the Jews find written in their Torah, just as it is written in the Qur'an that he is a prophet."]]

It was also said: he is a prophet from the Children of Israel who believed, ﴿and you were arrogant, and you did not believe﴾. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verses 11–14:

﴿And those who disbelieved﴾ from among the Jews, ﴿said of those who believed: "Had it been [the religion of Muhammad (ﷺ)] [[Addition from "B".]] ﴿good, they would not have preceded us to it."﴾ Meaning ʿAbdullah ibn Salam and his companions.

Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning the polytheists of Makkah. They said: "If what Muhammad calls us to were good, so-and-so and so-and-so would not have preceded us to it." [[See: al-Tabari: 26/13; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/59; al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/440.]]

al-Kalbi said: "Those who disbelieved" were Asad and Ghatafan. They said to "those who believed," meaning Juhaynah and Muzaynah: "If what Muhammad brought were good, the shepherds of the goats would not have preceded us to it." [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/59.]]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And since they have not been guided by it﴾ meaning by the Qur'an, as the people of faith have been guided by it, ﴿they will say: "This is an ancient lie."﴾ Just as they said, "They are the myths of the ancients." ١٢٣/أ

﴿And before it﴾ meaning before the Qur'an, ﴿the Book of Moses﴾ meaning the Torah, ﴿as a guide﴾ to be followed, ﴿and a mercy﴾ from Allah for those who believed in it. Both words are in the accusative as circumstantial clauses (ḥāl), according to al-Kisa'i. Abu ʿUbaydah said: there is an implied element in it, meaning "We made it a guide and a mercy." In the speech there is an omitted element, its estimated form being: "And the Book of Moses preceded it as a guide, and they were not guided by it," just as He said in the first verse: "And since they have not been guided by it."

﴿And this is a Book confirming﴾ meaning the Qur'an confirms the books that came before it, ﴿in Arabic tongue﴾ — accusative as a circumstantial clause; it is also said to mean "in an Arabic language." ﴿To warn those who have wronged﴾ meaning the polytheists of Makkah. The people of the Hijaz, Syria and Ya'qub recited "to warn" (*litundhira*) with a *ta'* addressing the Prophet (ﷺ), while the others recited it with a *ya'* meaning the Book. ﴿And good tidings for the doers of good﴾ — "good tidings" (*bushra*) is in the nominative position, meaning: this is a Book confirming and [it is] good tidings.

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast — there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein eternally, as a reward for what they used to do.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verses 18–19:

﴿Those are the ones against whom the Word has been justified﴾ [the verse]. Allah the Exalted informs that these people have been decreed the word of punishment, and ʿAbd al-Rahman [ibn ʿAwf] was a believer among the most excellent Muslims, so he is not one of those upon whom the word of punishment has been decreed.

The meaning of ﴿those against whom the Word has been justified﴾ is: punishment has become binding upon them. ﴿Among nations﴾ [with nations] [[Addition from "B".]] ﴿that passed away before them, of jinn and humankind. Indeed, they were losers.﴾

﴿And for each are degrees according to what they did.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) said: He means whoever embraced Islam earlier is more excellent than whoever lagged behind him, even by an hour. Muqatil said: For each there are virtues according to their deeds, and Allah will repay them the reward of their deeds.

It was also said: "For each" means, for each one of the two groups, the believers and the disbelievers, there are "degrees," that is, stations and ranks with Allah on the Day of Resurrection according to their deeds, and He will recompense them for them.

Ibn Zayd said concerning this verse: The degrees of the people of the Fire go downward, and the degrees of the people of Paradise go upward [[See: al-Qurtubi: 16/198.]].

﴿And that He may fully pay them﴾: Ibn Kathir, the people of Basra, and ʿAsim read it with the *ya'* (third person), and the rest read it with the *nun* (first person plural).

﴿Their deeds, and they will not be wronged.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 20:

﴿And on the Day when those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire﴾ it will be said to them: ﴿You squandered your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them﴾. Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir, Abu Ja'far and Ya'qub read "a-dhhabtum" (أَأَذْهَبْتُمْ) with the interrogative (istifham) particle, and Ibn 'Amir pronounces the two hamzas (yahmizu hamzatayn). The others read it without the interrogative, as a statement (khabar). Both readings are eloquent (fasih), because the Arabs use the interrogative to express reproach (tawbikh), and they also omit it, saying: "adhahabta fa-fa'alta kadha?" (Did you go and do such-and-such?).

﴿And you enjoyed them﴾ means: "Did you squander your good things," meaning the pleasures, "and enjoy them?" ﴿So today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation﴾, that is, the punishment in which there is disgrace (dhull) and shame (khizy), ﴿for what you used to be arrogant about﴾ [tatakabbarun] (the variant reading in brackets is supplied from copy "b") ﴿in the earth without right, and for what you used to defy (tafsuqun)﴾.

When Allah rebuked the disbelievers for enjoying good things in the world, the Prophet ﷺ and his companions and the righteous preferred to abstain from worldly pleasures, hoping for the reward of the Hereafter.

I said: "O Messenger of Allah, supplicate Allah that He may widen (provision) for your community, for Persia and Rome have been given abundance, and they do not worship Allah." He said: "Those are a people whose good things have been hastened to them in the life of this world." (1479): 2/1105-1108; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/270-271. "Rimal" is a weave of palm fronds; one says: "ramalt al-hasir" and "armalt".]

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verses 21–22:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And mention the brother of 'Ad﴾, meaning Hud, peace be upon him, ﴿when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "al-Ahqaf" is a valley between Oman and Mahra.

Muqatil said: The dwellings of 'Ad were in Yemen, in Hadramawt, at a place called "Mahra," and the Mahri camels are attributed to it. They were people of mobile pillars (tents), moving in the spring, and when the pasture dried up they returned to their dwellings. They were from the tribe of Iram.

Qatadah said: We were told that 'Ad were tribes in Yemen, and that they were people of sand dunes overlooking the sea, in a land called "al-Shihr." "Al-Ahqaf" is the plural of "hiqf," which is a long, winding mass of sand. Ibn Zayd said: They are what stretches of sand become long like the shape of a mountain, without reaching the size of a mountain. al-Kisa'i said: They are what is rounded of sand.

﴿And warners had already passed away﴾, meaning messengers had gone, ﴿before him and after him﴾, meaning before Hud and after him, to their peoples, ﴿[saying]: Worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾

﴿They said: Have you come to us to turn us away﴾ [to divert us] [[addition from "B".]] ﴿from our gods?﴾, meaning from worshipping them. ﴿So bring us what you threaten us with﴾ [of the punishment] [[addition from "B".]] ﴿if you are of the truthful﴾, that the punishment will descend upon us.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verses 23–25:

﴿He said﴾ [Hud], ﴿"The knowledge is only with Allah"﴾, and He knows when the punishment will come to you. ﴿"And I convey to you what I have been sent with"﴾ of the revelation, ﴿"but I see you as a people who are ignorant."﴾

﴿Then when they saw it﴾, meaning what they were promised of the punishment, ﴿as a cloud approaching﴾, a cloud that spreads, meaning it appears in one direction of the sky and then covers the sky, ﴿facing their valleys﴾. A black cloud came out over them from a valley of theirs called "al-Mughith," and rain had been withheld from them. When they saw it, they rejoiced, ﴿and said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain."﴾ Allah the Exalted says: ﴿"Rather, it is what you were hastening for: a wind in which is a painful punishment."﴾ So the wind began to carry the tent and carry the howdah until it was seen as if it were a locust.

﴿It destroys everything﴾ that it passed over, of the men of 'Ad and their property, ﴿by the command of its Lord﴾ [[Omitted from manuscript "A".]]. The first sign by which they knew that it was a punishment was that they saw what was outside their homes, the men and the livestock, being carried by the wind between the sky and the earth. So they entered their houses and closed their doors, but the wind came, tore off their doors and threw them down. Allah commanded the wind, and it poured the sand over them, so they remained under the sand for seven nights and eight days, moaning. Then Allah commanded the wind, and it cleared the sand away from them, lifted them up, and threw them into the sea.

Imam Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Abu Nu'aym 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Hasan al-Isfarayini informed us: Abu 'Awana Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Hafiz informed us: Yunus informed us: Ibn Wahb informed us: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed us: al-Nadr narrated to him from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from 'A'isha, that she said: "I never saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughing so fully that I could see the whiteness of his uvula. Rather, when he saw a cloud or a wind, it was recognized in his face." I said, "O Messenger of Allah, when people see a cloud they rejoice, hoping that it will bring rain, but when you see it, the dislike is recognized in your face." He said: "O 'A'isha, what assures me that it does not contain a punishment? A people were punished by the wind, and a people saw the punishment and said: 'This is a cloud bringing us rain'," the verse [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Istisqa', chapter on seeking refuge when seeing wind and cloud, and rejoicing in rain, no. 899: 2/616–617.]].

﴿So they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings﴾. 'Asim, Hamza and Ya'qub read "yura" (يُرَى) with a dammah on the ya', and "masakinuhum" (مَسَاكِنُهُمْ) with a raf' (nominative) on the nun, meaning: nothing was seen except their dwellings. The others (the remaining readers) read it with a ta' (تَرَى) and a fatha on it, and "masakinahum" (مَسَاكِنَهُمْ) with a nasb (accusative), meaning: you, O Muhammad, do not see anything except their dwellings. This is because the inhabitants and the cattle were swept away by the wind, so none remained except Hud and those who believed with him.

﴿Thus We recompense the criminal people.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verses 26–28:

﴿And We had certainly established them in that wherein We have not established you﴾, meaning: in that wherein We did not establish you, of physical strength, long life, and abundance of wealth.

Al-Mubarrad said: "Ma" in His saying "fima" (in that which) is in the sense of "alladhi" (that which), and "in" is in the sense of "ma" (not). Its construction is: "And We had certainly established them in that alladhi ma (which not) We established you in."

﴿And We had made for them hearing, sight, and hearts, but their hearing, their sight, and their hearts availed them nothing at all, since they used to deny the signs of Allah, and there encompassed them that which they used to mock.﴾

﴿And We had certainly destroyed the cities around you﴾, O people of Makkah, ﴿of the towns﴾, such as the Hijr of Thamud, the land of Sodom, and their like, ﴿and We made the signs clear﴾, meaning the proofs and the clear evidences, ﴿that they might return﴾ from their disbelief, but they did not return, so We destroyed them. This is a warning to the polytheists of Makkah.

﴿Why then did they not help them﴾, that is, why did they not (help)? ﴿those whom they had taken as gods besides Allah, as a means of nearness﴾, meaning the idols, which they took as gods, seeking nearness to Allah ʿAzza wa Jall through them. "Al-qurban" (the means of nearness) is everything by which one seeks nearness to Allah ʿAzza wa Jall. Its plural is "qarabin," like "al-ruhban" (the monks) and "al-rahabin."

﴿Nay, they vanished from them.﴾ Muqatil said: Nay, the gods vanished from them, and did not benefit them when the punishment descended upon them. ﴿And that was their falsehood﴾, meaning their lie, which they used to say: that they would bring them near to Allah ʿAzza wa Jall and intercede for them, ﴿and what they used to invent﴾, meaning what they used to lie about, that they were gods.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verse 29 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And [mention] when We turned toward you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an﴾, and so on. The exegetes (mufassirun) said: When Abu Talib died, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out alone to Ta'if, seeking support and protection from Thaqif against his people. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached Ta'if, he came to a group of Thaqif, and they were then the chiefs and nobles of Thaqif. They were three brothers: Abd Yalil, Mas'ud, and Habib, the sons of [Amr ibn] [[Omitted in "A".]] Umayr. One of them had a woman from Quraysh from the clan of Banu Jumah. He sat with them, called them to Allah, and spoke to them about what he had come for: support for Islam and standing with him against those of his people who opposed him.

One of them said to him: "He would tear the coverings of the Ka'bah, if Allah had sent you!" Another said: "Did Allah find no one else to send but you?" The third said: "By Allah, I will never speak a word to you! If you are truly a messenger from Allah, as you claim, then you are too great a matter for me to answer you; and if you are lying about Allah, then it is not fitting for me to speak to you."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose from their presence, having despaired of any good from Thaqif, and said to them: "Since you have done what you have done, keep my matter hidden [[Omitted in "B".]]." He disliked that his people should learn of it, lest it increase them in opposition to him. But they did not do so. They incited their foolish ones and their slaves against him, who cursed him and shouted at him, until the people gathered around him. They forced him against a wall belonging to Utbah and Shaybah, the sons of Rabi'ah, who were inside it. The foolish ones of Thaqif and those who had followed him turned back. He then went to the shade of a grapevine and sat in it, while the two sons of Rabi'ah watched him and saw what he suffered from the foolish ones of Thaqif.

The Prophet ﷺ met that woman from Banu Jumah, and he said to her: "What have we suffered from your in-laws?"

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had calmed down, he said: "O Allah, I complain to You of my weakness of strength, my scarcity of resources, and my lowliness before people. You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. You are the Lord of the weak, and You are my Lord. To whom will You entrust me? To a distant stranger who scowls at me, or to an enemy whom You have given power over my affair? If You are not angry with me, I do not mind; but Your well-being is more expansive for me. I seek refuge in the light of Your Face, by which the darknesses are illuminated and by which the affairs of this world and the Hereafter are set right, from Your wrath descending upon me or Your displeasure settling upon me. To You belongs the reproach until You are pleased; there is no power and no strength except through You."

When the two sons of Rabi'ah saw what he had suffered, their kinship was stirred for him. They called a Christian slave of theirs named Addas and said to him: "Take a bunch of grapes, put it on that platter, then go with it to that man and tell him to eat from it." Addas did so. Then he came with it and placed it before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ put out his hand, he said: "In the name of Allah," and then he ate. Addas looked at his face and then said: "By Allah, this is not the speech of the people of this land." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "What land are you from, Addas, and what is your religion?" He said: "I am a Christian, and I am a man from the people of Nineveh." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "From the town of the righteous man Yunus ibn Matta?" He said to him: "And what would you know of Yunus ibn Matta?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "That was my brother; he was a prophet, and I am a prophet." Addas then threw himself upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, kissed his head, his hands, and his feet.

He said: One of the two sons of Rabi'ah said to his companion: "As for your slave, he has corrupted him for you." When Addas came to them, they said to him: "Woe to you, Addas! Why do you kiss the head of this man, and his hands and feet?" He said: "O my master, there is nothing on earth better than this man. He has told me of a matter that none knows except a prophet." They said: "Woe to you, Addas! Let him not turn you away from your religion, for your religion is better than his."

Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ departed from Ta'if returning to Makkah, having despaired of any good from Thaqif. When he reached Nakhlah, he stood in the middle of the night to pray, and a company of jinn from the people of Nasibin, [and] of Yemen, passed by him and listened to him. When he finished his prayer, they turned back to their people as warners, having believed and responded to what they had heard. Allah related their story to him, and He said: "And [mention] when We turned toward you a company of the jinn..." [[Mentioned by Ibn Hisham in al-Sirah: 1/419-422, and al-Tabari in al-Tarikh: 2/344-347. al-Tabarani narrated a portion of it, which is: "O Allah, to You I complain..." al-Haythami said in al-Majma': 6/35: "In it is Ibn Ishaq, who is a mudallis (one who conceals defects in his chain) but trustworthy, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy." See also: Fiqh al-Sirah by al-Ghazali, edited by al-Albani, p. (137), and refer to what the scholar al-Lucknawi wrote on the authentication of Ibn Ishaq and the acceptance of his narration in his book: "Imam al-Kalam fima yata'allaq bil-qira'ah khalf al-imam," pp. 280-291, edited by Uthman Jum'ah Dumayriyah.]].

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us; Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us; Musaddad narrated to us; Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet ﷺ set out with a group of his companions, intending for the market of Ukaz, and the devils had been prevented from the news of the heavens; meteors were sent against them, so the devils returned to their people. They said: "What is the matter with you?" They said: "We have been prevented from the news of the heavens, and meteors have been sent against us." They said: "Only something new has happened that has come between you and the news of the heavens. So strike the east and west of the earth, and look into what has come between you and the news of the heavens." Those who had headed toward Tihamah turned back to the Prophet ﷺ while he was at Nakhlah, intending for the market of Ukaz, and he was leading his companions in the Fajr prayer. When they heard the Qur'an, they listened to it and said: "By Allah, this is what has come between you and the news of the heavens!" Then they returned to their people and said: "O our people, 'We have heard a wondrous Qur'an, guiding to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord'" [al-Jinn: 2]. Then Allah revealed to His Prophet: "Say: It has been revealed to me that a company of the jinn listened" [al-Jinn: 1]. What was revealed to him was only the words of the jinn [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Adhan, chapter on reciting audibly in the Fajr prayer: 2/253, and in the Tafsir: 8/669.]].

It is also narrated: When they returned with the meteors, Iblis sent out his expeditions to learn the news. The first expedition he sent was a riding party from the people of Nasibin, and they were the nobles and chiefs of the jinn. He sent them toward Tihamah.

Abu Hamzah [al-Thumali] [[In "A" it reads al-Yamani; what we have written is the correct reading.]] said: It has reached us that they were from the Shaysaban, who are the most numerous of the jinn and make up the main part of Iblis's armies. When they returned, they said: "We have heard a wondrous Qur'an."

A group said: Rather, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to warn the jinn, call them to Allah the Exalted, and recite the Qur'an to them. So Allah turned toward him a company of jinn from the people of Nineveh and gathered them for him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been commanded to recite the Qur'an to the jinn tonight, so which of you will follow me?" They lowered their heads. Then he invited them a second time, and they lowered their heads. Then he invited them a third time, and they lowered their heads. Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud followed him. Abd Allah said: No one else was present with him but me. We set out until, when we were above Makkah, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ entered a ravine called the Shi'b al-Hajun, and he drew a line for me and commanded me to sit within it, saying: "Do not leave it until I return to you." Then he went on until he stood and began the Qur'an. I began to see things like vultures swooping, and I heard a loud clamour, until I feared for the Prophet of Allah ﷺ. Many black shapes surrounded him and came between me and him, so that I could no longer hear his voice. Then they began to disperse like pieces of cloud, departing. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished at dawn and came to me and said: "Did you sleep?" I said: "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah. I had resolved many times to call for help from the people until I heard you striking them with your staff, saying: 'Sit down!'" He said: "If you had come out, I would not have been safe for you from some of them snatching you away." Then he said: "Did you see anything?" I said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, I saw men, black, with white garments tucked up." He said: "Those were the jinn of Nasibin. They asked me for provisions, and provisions are food. So I provided them with every dry bone, dung, and droppings."

He said: They said: "O Messenger of Allah, people find them filthy." So the Prophet ﷺ forbade cleaning oneself with bones and dung.

He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, and how does that benefit them?" He said: "They do not find a bone except that they find meat upon it on the day it was eaten, and they do not find a dropping except that they find its grain in it on the day it was eaten." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I heard a loud clamour?" He said: "The jinn disputed over a slain man who had been killed among them, so they brought their dispute to me, and I judged between them with truth." He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ relieved himself, then came to me and said: "Do you have water with you?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have a water-skin with some date-nabidh (date wine) in it." He asked for it, and I poured it over his hand, and he performed ablution and said: "A good date and pure water" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the Tahara, chapter: Ablution with nabidh: 1/82, and al-Tirmidhi in the Tahara, chapter: What has come about ablution with nabidh: 1/292. Abu Isa said: "This hadith is only narrated from Abu Zayd, from Abd Allah, from the Prophet ﷺ, and Abu Zayd is an unknown man according to the people of hadith; no narration is known from him other than this hadith. Some people of knowledge held the view of performing ablution with nabidh, among them Sufyan al-Thawri and others." Ibn Majah in the Tahara, chapter on ablution with nabidh, no. (384), 1/135, said: "The hadith revolves around Abu Zayd, who is unknown according to the people of hadith." Also Imam Ahmad: 1/450; Abd al-Razzaq: 1/238; Ibn al-Mundhir in al-Awsat: 1/256. See also: Nasb al-Rayah by al-Zayla'i: 1/137-138; al-Awsat by Ibn al-Mundhir: 1/253-257.]].

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that when Ibn Mas'ud came to Kufah, he saw old men with gray hair from the Zutt, and they startled him when he saw them. He said: "Show yourselves!" It was said to him: "These are a people from the Zutt." He said: "How much they resemble the company who turned toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ" [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad: 1/455, and al-Tabari: 26/32.]], meaning the jinn.

Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us; Abd al-Ghaffar ibn Muhammad informed us; Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to us; Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us; Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us; Abd al-A'la narrated to us; Dawud, who is Ibn Abi Hind, narrated to us, from Amir, who said: I asked Alqamah: "Was Ibn Mas'ud present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the night of the jinn?" Alqamah said: I asked Ibn Mas'ud, and I said: "Was any of you present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the night of the jinn?" He said: "No. But we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one night, and we lost him, so we searched for him in the valleys and the ravines. We said: 'He has been carried off or assassinated.' We spent the worst night any people ever spent. When we woke in the morning, behold, he came from the direction of Hira. We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we lost you, we searched for you and did not find you, so we spent the worst night any people ever spent.' He said: 'The caller of the jinn came to me, so I went with him and recited the Qur'an to them.'"

He said: Then he took us along and showed us their traces and the traces of their fires.

قَالَ: وَسَأَلُوهُ الزَّادَ، فَقَالَ: "لَكُمْ كُلُّ عَظْمٍ ذُكِرَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ يَقَعُ فِي أَيْدِيكُمْ أَوْفَرَ مَا يَكُونُ لَحْمًا، وَكُلُّ بَعْرَةٍ عَلَفٌ لِدَوَابِّكُمْ". فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ): "فَلَا تَسْتَنْجُوا بِهِمَا فَإِنَّهُمَا طَعَامُ إِخْوَانِكُمْ مِنَ الْجِنِّ". [[أخرجه مسلم في الصلاة، باب الجهر بالقراءة في الصبح، والقراءة على الجن برقم: (٤٥٠) : ١ / ٣٣٢.]]

وَرَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حُجْرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ دَاوُدَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ: "وَآثَارُ نِيرَانِهِمْ". [[أخرجه مسلم في الموضع السابق.]]

قَالَ الشَّعْبِيُّ: "وَسَأَلُوهُ الزَّادَ، وَكَانُوا مِنْ جِنِّ الْجَزِيرَةِ" إِلَى آخِرِ الْحَدِيثِ، مِنْ قَوْلِ الشَّعْبِيِّ، مُفَصَّلًا مِنْ حَدِيثِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ. [[أخرجه مسلم في الموضع السابق.]]

قَوْلُهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: ﴿وَإِذْ صَرَفْنَا إِلَيْكَ نَفَرًا مِنَ الْجِنِّ يَسْتَمِعُونَ الْقُرْآنَ﴾ [﴿And when We turned towards you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an﴾]. اخْتَلَفُوا فِي عَدَدِ ذَلِكَ النَّفَرِ، فَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: كَانُوا سَبْعَةً مِنْ جِنِّ نَصِيبِينَ، فَجَعَلَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) رُسُلًا إِلَى قَوْمِهِمْ. وَقَالَ آخَرُونَ: كَانُوا تِسْعَةً. [[انظر: الطبري: ٢٦ / ٣٠-٣١. وذكر الهيثمي في المجمع عدة روايات عن ابن عباس لكنها ضعيفة، انظر المجمع: ٧ / ١٠٦.]] وَرَوَى عَاصِمٌ عَنْ زِرِّ بْنِ حُبَيْشٍ: كَانَ زَوْبَعَةُ مِنَ التِّسْعَةِ الَّذِينَ اسْتَمَعُوا الْقُرْآنَ.

﴿فَلَمَّا حَضَرُوهُ قَالُوا أَنْصِتُوا﴾ [﴿When they attended it, they said, "Be silent!"﴾]. قَالُوا: "صَهٍ" [ṣahin, an Arabic interjection meaning "Be silent!" or "Hush!"]. [[قال الهيثمي في المجمع: ٧ / ١٠٦: رواه البزار ورجاله ثقات، لكن بلفظ (سبعة) بدلا من (تسعة).]]

وَرُوِيَ فِي الْحَدِيثِ: "أَنَّ الْجِنَّ ثَلَاثَةُ أَصْنَافٍ: صِنْفٌ لَهُمْ أَجْنِحَةٌ يَطِيرُونَ بِهَا فِي الْهَوَاءِ، وَصِنْفٌ حَيَّاتٌ وَكِلَابٌ، وَصِنْفٌ يَحُلُّونَ وَيَظْعَنُونَ". [[صححه الحاكم: ٢ / ٤٥٦ على شرط الشيخين، وابن حبان برقم: (٢٠٠٧) ص (٤٩٢) من موارد الظمآن، وأخرجه البيهقي في الأسماء والصفات: ٢ / ١٣٠، والطحاوي في مشكل الآثار: ٤ / ٩٥-٩٦. قال الهيثمي في المجمع: ٨ / ٣٦: "رواه الطبراني، ورجاله وثقوا وفي بعضهم خلاف". وعزاه ابن حجر في المطالب العالية: ٣ / ٢١٨ لأبي يعلي، وصححه الألباني في "صحيح الجامع الصغير" ٣ / ٨٥.]]

فَلَمَّا حَضَرُوهُ قَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ: "أَنْصِتُوا وَاسْكُتُوا لِنَسْتَمِعَ إِلَى قِرَاءَتِهِ، فَلَا يَحُولُ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ الِاسْتِمَاعِ شَيْءٌ"، فَأَنْصَتُوا وَاسْتَمَعُوا الْقُرْآنَ، حَتَّى كَادَ يَقَعُ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ مِنْ شِدَّةِ حِرْصِهِمْ.

﴿فَلَمَّا قُضِيَ﴾ [﴿When it was concluded﴾] أَيْ: فَرَغَ مِنْ تِلَاوَتِهِ، ﴿وَلَّوْا إِلَى قَوْمِهِمْ﴾ [﴿they turned back to their people﴾] أَيِ: انْصَرَفُوا إِلَيْهِمْ، ﴿مُنْذِرِينَ﴾ [﴿as warners﴾] أَيْ: مُخَوِّفِينَ، دَاعِينَ بِأَمْرِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ (ﷺ).

He said, citing Ata: Their religion was Judaism, which is why they said: "We have heard a Book revealed after Musa (Moses)" [[See: al-Qurtubi, 16/217; Zad al-Masir, 7/390.]].

﴿O our people, respond to the caller of Allah﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿and believe in him; He will forgive you of your sins﴾. The word "min" (from) here is extra (silah), meaning "your sins," ﴿and will protect you from a painful punishment﴾. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: About seventy men from the jinn among their people responded to them. They returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and met him at al-Batha, and he recited the Qur'an to them and commanded and forbade them. [[See: al-Qurtubi, 16/217.]] This indicates that he (ﷺ) was sent to both jinn and humankind.

Muqatil said: No prophet before him was sent to both humankind and jinn together [[See: al-Qurtubi, 16/217.]].

The scholars differed regarding the ruling on believing jinn [[See: al-Qurtubi, 16/217-218; Tariq al-Hijratayn by Ibn al-Qayyim, pp. 323-324; Lawami' al-Anwar al-Bahiyya by al-Saffarini, 2/222-223. Al-Shibli al-Nu'mani also wrote a book comprehensively covering the rulings on jinn, titled "Ahkam al-Marjan fi Ahkam al-Jann."]]. One group said: They have no reward except being saved from the Fire. They interpreted His saying, "He will forgive you of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment," accordingly. Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, held this view.

Sufyan related from Layth, who said: The reward of the jinn is that they are protected from the Fire, and then they are told: "Become dust." This is like the beasts.

From Abu al-Zinad, who said: When judgment is passed among people, the believing jinn are told: "Return to dust," and they return to dust. At that point the disbeliever will say: "Would that I were dust" [An-Naba: 40].

Others said: They will have reward for good deeds just as they will have punishment for evil deeds, like humankind. Malik and Ibn Abi Layla held this view.

Jarir related from al-Dahhak: The jinn enter Paradise and eat and drink.

Al-Naqqash mentioned in his tafsir a report that they enter Paradise. It was asked: Do they partake of its delights? He said: Allah inspires them with His glorification and remembrance, and they derive from its pleasure what the children of Adam derive from the delights of Paradise. Artat ibn al-Mundhir said: I asked Damrah ibn Habib: Do the jinn have reward? He said: Yes, and he recited: "No man or jinn has touched them before" [Ar-Rahman: 74], and said: So the human women belong to humans, and the jinn women to jinn.

Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said: The believing jinn are around Paradise, in its outskirts and courtyards, but they are not inside it.

He said, citing Ata: Their religion was Judaism, which is why they said: "We have heard a Book revealed after Musa (Moses)" [[See: al-Qurtubi, 16/217; Zad al-Masir, 7/390.]].

And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah, [then] he cannot escape [Allah] on earth ﴿And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah, he is not one who can escape on earth﴾: he does not make Allah powerless so that He misses him. ﴿And he has no protectors besides Him﴾: helpers who would prevent him from Allah. ﴿Those are in clear error﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 46, verses 33–35:

﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and did not tire in creating them, is able to give life to the dead?﴾ "Did not tire" means He was not incapable of bringing them into being. ﴿Able﴾ is the reading of the common readers (al-'ammah). They differed about the reason the preposition bi (ba') enters it. Abu 'Ubaydah and al-Akhfash said: the ba' is redundant (za'idah) for emphasis, as in the saying "tanbutu bi-l-duhn" (it grows with oil).

Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: the Arabs insert the ba' in interrogation accompanied by negation, so they say: "ma azunnuka bi-qa'im" (I do not think you are standing).

Ya'qub read "yaqdir" with the ya', as a verb. Abu 'Ubaydah preferred the reading of the common readers, because in the reading of 'Abd Allah it is "qadir" without ba'.

﴿Yes, indeed; He is able to do everything.﴾

﴿On the Day when those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire﴾, it will be said to them, ﴿Is this not the truth?﴾ They will say, ﴿Yes, by our Lord.﴾ He says, meaning: it will be said to them, ﴿Taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve.﴾

﴿So be patient as the steadfast ones among the messengers were patient﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: those of resolve (dhawu al-hazm). Al-Dahhak said: those of determination and patience (dhawu al-jidd wa al-sabr).

They differed about who they are. Ibn Zayd said: all the messengers were ulu al-'azm; Allah did not send a prophet except that he had resolve, prudence, sound judgment and perfect intellect. The "min" (from) is inserted for classification (lil-tajnis), not for partition (lil-tab'id), as one says: "I bought robes of silk (khazz) and mantles of cloth (bazz)."

Some said: all the prophets were ulu al-'azm except Yunus ibn Matta, because of a hastiness that came from him. Do you not see that it was said to the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾?

Others said: they are the chosen messengers mentioned in Surat al-An'am, and they are eighteen, based on His saying after mentioning them: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance﴾ [al-An'am: 90].

Al-Kalbi said: they are those who were commanded to wage jihad and who openly confronted the enemies of the religion.

It was also said: they are six: Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut, Shu'ayb and Musa, peace be upon them, and they are mentioned in sequence in Surat al-A'raf and al-Shu'ara'.

Muqatil said: they are six: Nuh, who was patient over the harm of his people; Ibrahim, who was patient over the fire; Ishaq, who was patient over being sacrificed; Ya'qub, who was patient over the loss of his son and the loss of his sight; Yusuf, who was patient over the well and the prison; and Ayyub, who was patient over affliction.

Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: they are Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and 'Isa, the bearers of the law-giving (ashab al-shara'i'), so with Muhammad ﷺ they are five.

I say: Allah mentioned them specifically in His saying: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and 'Isa son of Maryam﴾ [al-Ahzab: 7], and in His saying: ﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Nuh﴾ [al-Shura: 13].
